explanation: Clownfish start life as males. Each group is led by a breeding female, and if she dies, her male partner changes sex and takes her place.

claims.text: A male clownfish can change sex to become female.
A clownfish group is led by a breeding female; if she dies, the breeding male changes sex and replaces her.

writerNotes: Self-check (guide 9.3), all eleven codes confirmed true. The selfCheck field itself is left out because the CNT-1 item schema refuses it as an unknown key, so the codes are recorded here. lint: content:check reports no errors and no warnings for this item. claims: three listed. c1 is high because it is the key of a counterintuitive item, so C26 sets it high; the tooling's riskReason enum has no counterintuitive value yet (guide v1.1 adds one), so checker_doubt stands in for it. c2 and c3 are standard marine biology. datasets: no pinned dataset in content/datasets/manifest.json covers animal or plant biology, so none applies and every high-risk claim needs web evidence from checker A. rivalTest: argued for false: it sounds like fiction, but clownfish are well-documented sequential hermaphrodites that change from male to female. No reading makes the statement false. volatility: evergreen, a settled fact that cannot change; no time words, and nothing rests on knowledge newer than mid-2026. regional: clownfish are famous worldwide from aquariums and films. style: Oxford spelling, plain hyphens only, explanation of 26 words. myths: screened against content/reference/myths.json; no entry matches. mystery and encore: nothing of either kind in a true/false item. doubts: none.

evidence.summaryExcerpt: Clownfish are protandrous. Clownfish are protandrous sequential hermaphrodites: the young fish are male. The sex change is usually triggered socially rather than by size. When the female disappears, the breeding male changes sex and takes her place while the others move up the hierarchy.
